key_concepts: Organisms are classified by physical characteristics from domain to species
Taxonomic hierarchy: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
Domain is the largest category; species is the smallest group of organisms that can reprod
Six-kingdom system includes Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, Protist, Fungi, Plant, and Animal
Scientific names use binomial nomenclature with genus first and species second
Scientific names are Latin or latinized, italicized or underlined, with genus capitalized
Carolus Linnaeus first named and classified plants and other organisms
Three-domain system divides prokaryotes into Archaea and Bacteria and retains Eukarya
Archaebacteria are microscopic, lack nucleus and organelles, and live in extreme environme
Species are groups whose members can mate and produce fertile offspring
Plants can be vascular or nonvascular based on vessels for food and water transport
Fishes, birds, mammals, reptiles, and amphibians are vertebrates
